identity.one_liner: Considered, small-batch fashion in natural fibres for people who buy less but buy better.
identity.target_customer: 28-45 year old urban professionals who value craftsmanship and provenance over trend cycles; low purchase frequency, high average order value, researches before buying.
value_props: Made-to-last construction, not seasonal trend cycles

tone.voice_notes: Reads like a design journal, not an ad. Leads with craft and material story before price or promotion.

competitors.name: Nicobar
competitors.positioning_note: Closest direct competitor, similar handloom/considered-design ethos.

customers.summary: Skews premium and loyal-core: low discount-code usage, high AOV, low cart-abandonment, values exclusivity over price.

history.title: Loom & Aster founded
history.summary: Launched with a single natural-dye linen capsule sold via a waitlist.

history.title: Featured in design press
history.summary: First editorial feature on the brand's handloom sourcing story.

history.title: Restock-waitlist mechanic introduced
history.summary: Small-batch drops paired with a public waitlist to signal demand ahead of restock.

history.title: First studio store opened
history.summary: Opened a single appointment-only studio store in a metro city.

insights.observation: Founder-narrated craft videos and real-customer styling clips outperformed polished studio lookbook images on engagement and dwell time across the last two seasonal launches.
A fit-guide video embedded on the PDP measurably reduced cart abandonment for first-time buyers unfamiliar with the brand's relaxed sizing.
Leading with fabric-sourcing/maker-story, not price, was the strongest lever converting price-sensitive browsers to premium buyers.
Small-batch drops paired with a public restock waitlist reliably sold out and produced a visible demand signal for the next batch size.
